chunks: Hadith 4099 — Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who took as collateral for his money a piece of land or a house, both of which had abundant yield.

He عليه السلام said: It is upon the one who took the land and the house as collateral for his money to calculate what he took from the yield for the owner of the land and the house, and deduct it from the debt owed to him.

key_terms.أَرْضًا: a piece of land given as collateral
key_terms.ارْتَهَنَ: to take something in pledge or as collateral
key_terms.الدَّيْنِ: the debt owed to the creditor
key_terms.رَهَنَ: to pledge or place property as collateral
key_terms.غَلَّةٌ: yield, produce, or income generated from the property

ai.seo_question: If a creditor benefits from the yield of pledged land or a house, must that value be deducted from the debt?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning pledged property that produces yield. If the creditor benefits from the produce of the mortgaged land or house, that benefit must be counted and deducted from the debtor's outstanding debt. It reflects fairness in financial dealings and the protection of the owner's rights.
